text:
alex_liu: Quick q — do we have a concise spec that tells clients how to distinguish transient vs terminal errors? i.e., when clients should retry vs stop and bubble to users.

maria-g: We have notes scattered across the error-mapping RFC but no single, client-facing contract. We should standardize a small surface: HTTP code + header + suggested action.

kevin: proposal from infra: treat 5xx, 429 (when Retry-After exists) as transient; 4xx that indicate auth/usage (401, 403 with quota_exhausted) as terminal. Also unknown/internal codes default to transient with limited retries.

kevin: example header idea: `X-Redwood-Error-Type: transient|terminal` and `X-Redwood-Action: retry|upgrade|contact_support|refresh_key`

alex_liu: That helps. What about routing fallbacks? sometimes we return a compatible smaller model or synthetic fallback payload — should that be terminal or transient?

sophie_w: If we return fallback payload successfully (200) that means app-level degradation not an error. But we should include `X-Redwood-Fallback: true` + `X-Redwood-Fallback-Reason` so clients can detect silent degradations. If we return 200 + null/placeholder because response couldn't be generated, that's a terminal failure we must avoid.

maria-g: Agreed. Also need guidance for SDKs: recommended retry policy limited to 3 attempts, exponential backoff with jitter, and treat 429+Retry-After as authoritative. We should expose those defaults in SDKs and console.

ravi_p: From product side — console should show a new badge per route: "Transient Errors (1h)" and "Terminal Errors (1h)" and provide quick runbook links. If an endpoint has >3% terminal errors we trigger alert.

kevin: Telemetry items: `error_kind` (transient/terminal), `http_status`, `error_code` (redwood canonical), `retryable` boolean, and `fallback_used` boolean. That lets us slice by user-impacting vs recoverable.

alex_liu: Can someone write the exact header names and sample responses? I'll draft the client-facing paragraph for the API docs once we have them.

maria-g: Sample 429 transient response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Error-Type: transient
Retry-After: 12
X-Redwood-Action: retry

{ "error": { "type": "rate_limit", "message": "Rate limit exceeded", "quota_window": "minute" } }
```

maria-g: Sample terminal (quota exhausted) response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Error-Type: terminal
X-Redwood-Action: upgrade

{ "error": { "type": "quota_exhausted", "message": "Quota exhausted for project", "details": "upgrade plan or request quota increase" } }
```

kevin: For auth failures: 401 should be terminal with `X-Redwood-Action: refresh_key` and helpful error_code like `invalid_api_key` so clients can detect and open an auth flow.

alex_liu: What about retriable 5xx that happen during a canary rollback? If we're rolling back and we intentionally degrade, we shouldn't spam customer retries. Maybe set `X-Redwood-Action: fallback` or `throttle`?

sophie_w: We already have a canary header `X-Redwood-Canary: <id>` — infra can set `X-Redwood-Action: fallback` when we are intentionally returning a degraded-but-stable path. SDKs can surface a distinct event so UX teams can decide whether to show ephemeral warnings or hard errors.

ravi_p: UX note: default behaviour in our official SDKs should be conservative — auto-retry transient errors up to N times, but bubble terminal errors immediate with the `error.message` and a single console-runbook link. For web clients we should expose `retryable` flags so app devs can decide to hide or surface.

kevin: Implementation TODOs: infra to add headers + canonical `error_code`s, telemetry team to map events, SDKs team to implement default retry/backoff and surface the headers, docs team to publish client-facing guidance.

alex_liu: I'll draft a short RFC with header names and a decision table (status -> type -> action) — assigning myself. Can @maria-g and @kevin own the header payloads and telemetry mapping?

maria-g: yep, I'll pair with kevin tomorrow.

kevin: SG, will add telemetry fields and sample metrics.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for `error-contracts/v0.3` on infra-canary-2 — watch logs for spikes, will post updates. :rocket:

alex_liu: Thanks all. Plan: RFC by EOD Friday, small console badge mockups after that. If anyone has strong objections to header names, speak now.

sophie_w: minor ask — include `X-Redwood-Error-Version: 1` so we can evolve contract without breaking SDKs.

alex_liu: good call. adding to RFC.

ravi_p: Also add examples for edge cases: model fallback vs auth vs quota. I'll draft runbook copy once RFC lands.

alex_liu: awesome — closing out here. Thanks! :thumbsup:
